statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES (orange). Tail 26% has crossed above the block threshold into the elevated band.
recommendation: A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged for 13:30-15:00 UTC, covering the Nasdaq cash open and the first full cash hour, where observed one-way structure meets the opening auction. Conditional Tail returns below the block threshold from the 15:00 UTC hour onward as the opening imbalance is assumed to clear. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged.
headline: NQ extends to a fresh 29,753 session high with VIX, yields and crude all lower; near-extreme holding into the cash open moves Tail into the block band
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 29,738.50 (+1.65%) against a 29,271.00 prior open, with a session range of 29,247.75-29,753.25 that leaves price roughly 15 points below a high set within the last hour. That is a second consecutive hour of extension: the 12:32 UTC assessment recorded 29,664.00 against a 29,680.75 high, so the relief grind has continued to make new highs rather than stalling. Cross-assets remain aligned in the same direction. VIX is 15.48 (-12.6%) and trading near its 15.41 session low against a 17.20 prior close; the 10-year yield is 4.948% (-5.6bp) and the 2-year 4.675% (-5.2bp); WTI has slipped to $100.42 (-2.0%) and Brent to $102.66 (-3.0%) as Saudi Arabia works to restore roughly half the damaged East-West pipeline capacity within days. Delayed latest-session context shows all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductor names higher, with the semiconductor group averaging +2.8%, which confirms the breadth of the move without providing live price-path evidence. The 12:30 UTC data cluster resolved without a violent repricing: initial jobless claims came in at 196,000 against a 208,000 consensus, the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index printed 37.8 against 31.3 expected while cooling from 47.4, and housing starts were softer at 1.275 million. The combination that matters for path risk is persistent directional efficiency, holding near the session extreme, and full cross-asset alignment arriving at the 13:30 UTC cash open, which is the configuration most associated with opening-auction continuation and shallow pullbacks. Against that, yesterday's post-FOMC sell-off to 28,753.29 retraced into a flat close, volatility is decaying rather than expanding, and the move is a second-day relief grind rather than fresh repricing, which argues against a lethal no-retracement regime. Tail is therefore set at 26%, at the low end of the elevated band, with Stress easing to 57% and Confidence at 87% on current futures, volatility, rates, crude and verified macro evidence.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment stayed mostly in the low-to-watch Tail band, with one orange excursion to Tail 31% in the 19:00 UTC hour as the FOMC statement and the Warsh press conference drove a Nasdaq-100 sell-off toward 28,753.29. That move retraced into a flat cash close and Tail fell back to 16-20% overnight. Stress decayed steadily from the high 70s before the decision to the high 50s by midday as volatility normalised, yields eased below 5% and crude fell on Saudi pipeline repair guidance. The most recent nine hours have carried a trend-up mode with Tail climbing from 19% to 23% as the European relief grind extended without a meaningful retracement.
outlookSummary: The current 13:00 UTC hour and the 14:00 UTC hour carry Tail in the elevated band, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first full cash hour, with the 14:00 slot holding the conditional daily peak of 27. Conditional Tail then decays through the US afternoon as the opening imbalance is assumed to clear, rises modestly into the 19:00 UTC power hour, and falls into the low band after the 20:00 UTC cash close. Overnight slots sit at 16-18 on the absence of scheduled catalysts rather than on any observed structure. Conditional Tail firms back into the watch band through Friday's European session and into the US pre-open, where September quarterly index expiration and the 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release are the named checkpoints. Confidence declines with forecast distance because evidence quality degrades, not because the risk picture deteriorates.
